subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — plugin emission API and manifest policy

question: Should OpenClaw commit to this six-event taxonomy and manifest-authorized external-plugin emission model as a permanent public Plugin SDK security contract?
rationale: This choice defines third-party authority, operator trust semantics, manifest compatibility, payload-validation ownership, and long-term taxonomy support; implementation review cannot safely infer those commitments.

options.title: Sponsor a host-bound API
options.body: Adopt the direction only after replacing caller-selected authority with a host-created capability and completing manifest validation, documentation, and installed-plugin proof.

options.title: Keep emission core-only
options.body: Allow only trusted core emitters while evaluating whether an external plugin contract is needed later.

options.title: Decline the taxonomy
options.body: Avoid adding permanent public event and manifest surfaces and retain existing diagnostics or plugin-owned telemetry paths.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a host-bound API
recommendation.body: Adopt the direction only after replacing caller-selected authority with a host-created capability and completing manifest validation, documentation, and installed-plugin proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent plugin-manifest history and prior public product/security review make this the strongest available decision-routing candidate.
